## Description

<p>A peak element is an element that is strictly greater than its neighbors.</p>
<p>Given a <strong>0-indexed</strong> integer array <code>nums</code>, find a peak element, and return its index. If the array contains multiple peaks, return the index to <strong>any of the peaks</strong>.</p>
<p>You may imagine that <code>nums[-1] = nums[n] = -&infin;</code>. In other words, an element is always considered to be strictly greater than a neighbor that is outside the array.</p>
<p>You must write an algorithm that runs in <code>O(log n)</code> time.</p>
<p><strong class="example">Example 1:</strong></p>
<pre>
<strong>Input:</strong> nums = [1,2,3,1]
<strong>Output:</strong> 2
<strong>Explanation:</strong> 3 is a peak element and your function should return the index number 2.</pre>
<p><strong class="example">Example 2:</strong></p>
<pre>
<strong>Input:</strong> nums = [1,2,1,3,5,6,4]
<strong>Output:</strong> 5
<strong>Explanation:</strong> Your function can return either index number 1 where the peak element is 2, or index number 5 where the peak element is 6.</pre>
<p><strong>Constraints:</strong></p>
<ul>
	<li><code>1 &lt;= nums.length &lt;= 1000</code></li>
	<li><code>-2<sup>31</sup> &lt;= nums[i] &lt;= 2<sup>31</sup> - 1</code></li>
	<li><code>nums[i] != nums[i + 1]</code> for all valid <code>i</code>.</li>
</ul>

---
## Solution

If the question did not specifically ask for O(log n) time our simple solution would be loop over each element and see if that one is a local top. Worst case that is O(n). However we can do better. Since an element is always considered to be strictly greater than a neighbor that is outside the array; we can detect where the peak will be by looking to a next value and comparing it to a current one.

So let's say nums = [...,3,5,...] and we pick the element in the middle to check.

nums[m] = 3 is the middle of this array.

if we look at nums[m + 1] = 5. 

In this case we can tell that there is a peak at the right of the middle.

And otherwise if the next element is smaller, we know that there is a peak located on the left side or the middle.
<div>
<div class="excalidraw-svg excalidraw-dark" style="background-image:url(data:image/svg+xml;base64,);background-size:cover;background-repeat:no-repeat;width:907.3025512695312px;height:auto;aspect-ratio:3.1629085981290315;"></div>
<div class="excalidraw-svg excalidraw-light" style="background-image:url(data:image/svg+xml;base64,);background-size:cover;background-repeat:no-repeat;width:907.3025512695312px;height:auto;aspect-ratio:3.1629085981290315;"></div>
</div>

With that information at hand we can eliminate half of the array with each iteration with binary search and finding the peak thus O(log n).

```python
def find_peak(nums):
    l, r = 0, len(nums) - 1

    while l < r:
        m = (l + r) // 2
        if nums[m] > nums[m + 1]:
            r = m
        else:
            l = m + 1
            
    return r
            
nums = [1,2,1,3,5,6,4]
print(find_peak(nums))
```
